item.title: A Kleene-inspired sequent system for a minimal logic of evidence and truth
item.description: arXiv:2610.24203v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the proof theory of the logic of evidence and truth LETFm, with the aim of obtaining a sequent calculus consisting only of logical rules, suitable for a simple bottom-up decision procedure. We begin with G1f, a sequent system containing structural rules, which makes explicit the main difficulties in obtaining a fully logical and decidable calculus for LETFm. We then introduce G3f, a G3-style system obtained from by applying Kleene's trick, which absorbs contraction into the logical rules by adding the principal formula of the rule to its premises.
item.dc:creator: Nino Grandinetti, Abilio Rodrigues

item.title: Weakly uniform computable categoricity and function composition
item.description: arXiv:2610.24422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the definition of a weakly $X$-uniformly $Y$-computably categorical structure, relativizing a definition of Kudinov (1996), and show that this relativized notion is closely related to the 2-dimensional complexity of the pairs of partial functions $(f,g)$ with the property that the composition $g\circ f$ simulates convergent $\emptyset'$-oracle computations. We develop a general theory for computing via composition and use it to prove results about the surprisingly complex weakly uniform categoricity spectrum of the structure $(\omega,S)$ where $S(n)=n+1$. Namely, that $(\omega,S)$ is w.$X$.u.$Y$.c.c. for some $X\not\geq_T\emptyset'$ and $Y<_T\emptyset'$, but $(\omega,S)$ is not w.$X$.u.$Y$.c.c. for any $X<_T\emptyset'$ and $Y\not\geq_T\emptyset'$. We also construct a computably categorical structure that is not w.$\emptyset'$.u.c.c., but is w.$X$.u.c.c. for a set $X$ that is $\leq_T$-incomparable with $\emptyset'$.
item.dc:creator: Joey Lakerdas-Gayle

item.title: Short proof that Vop\v{e}nka's Principle is symmetrically stable
item.description: arXiv:2610.24570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that Vop\v{e}nka's Principle is stable under symmetric extensions. Recently, de Groot and Woloszyn [1] proved this fact. We found the proof of this theorem unnecessarily complicated. In this short note we prove the same statement. We direct the reader to [3] for an exposition on symmetric extensions.
item.dc:creator: Asaf Karagila

item.title: Model Theory of Products of Chains
item.description: arXiv:2610.24683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that regarding the model-theoretic properties of distributive lattices isomorphic to finite products of linear orders there is a significant symmetry: if ${\mathbb X}_i$, $i<n$ are linear orders of size $>1$, ${\mathcal T}:=\mathop{\rm Th}\nolimits (\prod _{i<n}{\mathbb X} _i)$ and ${\mathcal T}_i:=\mathop{\rm Th}\nolimits ({\mathbb X}_i)$, for $i<n$, then ${\mathcal T}$ is finitely axiomatizable (resp. atomic, small) iff ${\mathcal T}_i$, $i<n$, are finitely axiomatizable (resp. atomic, small); the countable atomic (resp. countably saturated) model of ${\mathcal T}$, if it exists, is the product of countable atomic (resp. countably saturated) models of ${\mathcal T}_i$; further, we describe all models of ${\mathcal T}$: ${\mathbb Y} \models {\mathcal T}$ iff ${\mathbb Y}\cong \prod _{i<n}{\mathbb Y}_i$, where ${\mathbb Y} _i \models {\mathcal T}_i$, for $i<n$, and show that ${\mathbb E} \preccurlyeq \prod _{i<n}{\mathbb X}_i$ iff ${\mathbb E} = \prod _{i<n}{\mathbb E}_i$, where ${\mathbb E}_i \preccurlyeq {\mathbb X}_i$, for $i<n$. ($I({\mathcal T},\omega)\in \{ 1,{\mathfrak{c}}\}$ was proved in a previous paper.) In addition, for each $n\in {\mathbb N}$ the class ${\mathcal C}_n$ of distributive lattices isomorphic to a direct product of $n$ linear orders of size $>1$ is first order definable.
item.dc:creator: Milo\v{s} S. Kurili\'{c}

item.title: The pattern of consistency strength for membership in a computably enumerable set
item.description: arXiv:2610.24919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every computable preorder relation on the natural numbers is the order of consistency strength for the membership assertions "$n\in A$" in some computably enumerable set $A$. Moreover, for every computably enumerable list of theories $T_0,T_1,T_2,\ldots$, each extending PA, there is a computably enumerable set $A$ such that each $T_n$ is equiconsistent over PA with the membership assertion $n\in A$. And similarly for both results when using instead the nonmembership assertions $n\notin A$.
item.dc:creator: Joel David Hamkins, Atticus Stonestrom

item.title: Equivalence of Restricted and Full Division
item.description: arXiv:2610.24976v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove over $\mathrm{PA}^{-}$ that the restricted Euclidean division principle $\mathrm{pa17}^{-}$, which asserts division only for co-prime pairs, is equivalent to the full principle $\mathrm{pa17}$. The proof uses a transformation that preserves the quotient in division with remainder to reduce an arbitrary division problem to one for a co-prime pair. This answers Visser's Open Question 8.29 and shows that the restricted principle has the same strength as full Euclidean division over $\mathrm{PA}^{-}$.
item.dc:creator: Naoya Kato

item.title: A sound pure type system with ranks as sorts and Type-in-Type
item.description: arXiv:2610.25085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a dependently typed pure type system that contains a circular axiom $s : s$ for a certain sort $s$ and is nonetheless strongly normalizing. Girard's paradox is avoided because our sorts are not closed under a $\Pi$-former: function types are placed in sorts according to their rank. Turns out that this system has a unique set of characteristics: it has similar normalization behaviour as STLC (so complexity of normalization is TOWER-complete) while at the same time allowing non-uniform representation of arbitrary elementary recursive functions; furthermore, it has a nontrivial set-theoretical model in ZF+GCH and allows to carry out nontrivial proof developments. Base normalization proof is surprisingly simple (modulo general metatheoretical properties of pure type systems) and has been fully formalized in vanilla Rocq (formerly Coq) without additional axioms.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Sokolov, Alexander Kuklev

item.title: Identity crisis on tightly $C^{(2)}$-compact cardinals
item.description: arXiv:2610.25099v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bagaria and Goldberg asked if $\kappa$ being tightly $C^{(n)}$-compact implies $\kappa\in C^{(n+1)}$ for natural numbers $n\ge 1$? Usuba gave a negative answer for $n=1$. In this paper we give a negative answer for $n=2$.
item.dc:creator: Fengju Zhang

item.title: Studying proof data with proof theory: the case of AI-generated mathematics
item.description: arXiv:2610.25357v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: I present a method for analyzing large collections of formally verified mathematical proofs (e.g. OpenAI's) grounded in some historical and philosophical musings on mathematics in the age of AI. Many of the quantities involved, such as the size of a proof term or the number of redundant steps, are already computed by work on improving automated provers, where they serve as targets. My aim is to turn them into measurements of proofs themselves: compared against a reference library and against each proof's own cut-free form, checked against theorems they must obey, and controlled for how the proofs were compiled. With these instruments, I measure how (much) machine-generated mathematics diverges from human mathematics, and find that AI-written formal proofs realize far less of the logical compression available to them than human mathematicians do (31% against 73% in mathlib, and 55% against 86% on proofs that call no automation). These figures are broadly in line with reports from those who build provers and proof-improvement tools that AI-written proofs are often longer than they need to be.
item.dc:creator: Safal Raman Aryal

item.title: Two Generalizations of the G_0 Dichotomy
item.description: arXiv:2610.25587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give classical proofs of the generalizations of the $\mathbb{G}_0$ dichotomy to $\kappa$-Souslin digraphs and uniformly analytic sequences of digraphs indexed by $\kappa^{\mathbb{N}}$.
item.dc:creator: B. Miller

item.title: Big Ramsey degrees and structures in relational languages
item.description: arXiv:2610.25715v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a precompact transfer theorem for big Ramsey structures and a uniform envelope theorem for valuation hypergraphs. These yield big Ramsey structures for generic injective relational structures in languages with finitely many symbols of each positive arity, answering the existence part of Problem 6.3.2 of Balko et al. (arXiv:2110.08409), and refute Conjecture 4.7 of Braunfeld et al. (arXiv:2301.13116). We also construct a finitely constrained free amalgamation class in a finite language of maximum arity three whose Fra\"iss\'e limit has infinite singleton big Ramsey degree, giving a negative answer to the existence question in Problem 6.3.3 of Balko et al.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Hu

item.title: Jumps and Iterated Jumps of Perfect Subtrees of Positive Trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.25769v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An infinite (binary) tree is \emph{positive} iff its set of paths is non-null. As an elementary observation, positives trees always have positive perfect subtrees. Given a positive tree of certain complexity, here we present several theorems concerning the distribution of the Turing jumps or iterated Turing jumps of (positive) perfect subtrees of the given tree in the universe of Turing degrees.
item.dc:creator: Wei Wang

item.title: On stable semilinear sets in ordered vector spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.26335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a general decomposition for regular closed semilinear sets, derived from a detailed study of their topological boundary. As an application, we characterize stable semilinear sets in ordered vector spaces over an ordered field, extending previous results of Hoffmann, Tran, and Ye.
item.dc:creator: Marcos Gir\'on

item.title: Well-ordering principles over recursive comprehension
item.description: arXiv:2610.26336v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a general result on the proof-theoretic strength of well-ordering principles in reverse mathematics. The novelty is that our result gives information over base theories as weak as $\mathsf{RCA}_0$, while previous results of Arai, Pakhomov-Walsh and Buriola-Weiermann required the stronger base theory $\mathsf{ACA}_0$. On the way, we strengthen a result of Carlucci-Mainardi-Rathjen about the ordinal analysis of theories of the form $\mathsf{RCA}_0+\text{``$\alpha$ is a well-order"}$.
item.dc:creator: Gabriele Buriola, Giacomo Cozzi, Antonia Dammrau, Anton Freund

item.title: Sublinear Michaux-Villemaire over $(\mathbb{N}, +, k^\mathbb{N})$
item.description: arXiv:2610.26409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1996, Michaux and Villemaire showed that any nontrivial expansion of $(\mathbb{N}, +)$ defines new unary sets. We conjecture that the same holds over the structure $(\mathbb{N}, +, k^\mathbb{N})$, and we prove a partial result in this direction. To do so, we first show that every nonempty sparse $k$-automatic set is a Presburger-definable image of some Cartesian power of $k^\mathbb{N}$. Using this characterization, we prove that if an expansion of $(\mathbb{N}, +, k^\mathbb{N})$ defines the same unary sets, then every set of sublinear growth definable in the expansion is already definable in $(\mathbb{N}, +, k^\mathbb{N})$.
item.dc:creator: Chris Schulz

item.title: Tactix: Towards a Programmable Strategy Interface for Flexible SAT Solving
item.description: arXiv:2610.24369v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern SAT solvers combine a rich repertoire of proof rules with sophisticated strategies that determine when and how to apply them. Often, the internal implementations are tightly coupled to particular strategies, making it inconvenient to define new strategies without changing solver internals. We present Tactix, a proof-producing sequential CDCL solver that incorporates a wide range of techniques in state-of-the-art solvers with a clean separation of proof rules from solving strategies. This separation enables a public interface through which users can invoke particular techniques, observe their effects, and program a wide range of solving strategies. The default strategy of Tactix is programmable over this interface and outperforms state-of-the-art solvers on benchmarks from the 2024--2026 SAT Competitions. We also use the interface to develop novel strategies tailored to challenging benchmarks from two application domains, which led to performance gains over strong baselines. We intend Tactix to serve as an infrastructure for designing and evaluating novel solving strategies. Finally, we also present a self-study of the AI-assisted development process behind Tactix.
item.dc:creator: Haoze Wu, Andr\'e Schidler, Armin Biere, Nina Narodytska

item.title: The Lattice of Coalition Logics between MCL and CL: Coatoms and Compact Meets
item.description: arXiv:2610.24466v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a fixed finite set $N$ of at least two agents, we investigate the lattice $L_N$ of coalition logics between minimal coalition logic (MCL) and classical coalition logic (CL), with extensions required to be structural. This lattice is order-dual to an interval in the subvariety lattice of Boolean coalition algebras. The eight basic extensions obtained by imposing seriality, independence of agents, and determinism form a Boolean cube under inclusion, but not a sublattice of $L_N$. Our main results concern coatoms and compact meets. First, finite critical coalition algebras, realized as complex algebras of finite general concurrent games, yield three infinite families of pairwise distinct coatoms containing seriality, distinguished by failures of independence, determinism, or both. An explicit splitting characterizes the unique coatom omitting seriality. Second, the meet of two basic extensions is compact if and only if the extensions are comparable. For incomparable pairs, no axiomatization of the meet can use formulas of uniformly bounded modal depth, even with infinitely many axioms. Consequently, $L_N$ and three natural principal intervals are non-coherent algebraic lattices. These results reveal lattice-theoretic phenomena beyond the inclusion order of the eight basic extensions.
item.dc:creator: Shanxia Wang, Yuqiang Dou

item.title: Ramsey expansions of $S$-metric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.26167v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $S\subseteq \mathbb R^+$ be a subset of positive reals. We say that a metric space is an $S$-metric space if the range of the metric is a subset of $S\cup \{0\}$. In 2007, Delhomm\'{e}, Laflamme, Pouzet, and Sauer characterized those sets $S$ for which the class of all finite $S$-metric spaces has the amalgamation property. Given an amalgamation class, a natural question is what its Ramsey expansion is. Ramsey expansions are known for classes of $S$-metric spaces for which $S\cup\{0\}$ carries a natural distance monoid structure, for example for $S=\mathbb Q^+$ or when $S$ is topologically closed. In this paper, we extend this result to all amalgamation classes of finite $S$-metric spaces, thereby completing the Ramsey-theoretic classification of amalgamation classes of finite $S$-metric spaces.
item.dc:creator: Jan Hubi\v{c}ka, Mat\v{e}j Kone\v{c}n\'{y}, Jaroslav Ne\v{s}et\v{r}il, Norbert Sauer

item.title: Suszko's Thesis and Many-valued Logical Structures
item.description: arXiv:2408.13769v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we try to formulate a definition of ''many-valued logical structure''. For this, we embark on a deeper study of Suszko's Thesis ($\mathbf{ST}$) and show that the truth or falsity of $\mathbf{ST}$ depends, at least, on the precise notion of semantics. We propose two different notions of semantics and three different notions of entailment. The first one helps us formulate a precise definition of inferentially many-valued logical structures. The second and the third help us to generalise Suszko Reduction and provide adequate bivalent semantics for monotonic and a couple of nonmonotonic logical structures. All these lead us to a closer examination of the played by language/metalanguage hierarchy vis-\'a-vis $\mathbf{ST}$. We conclude that many-valued logical structures can be obtained if the bivalence of all the higher-order metalogics of the logic under consideration is discarded, building formal bridges between the theory of graded consequence and the theory of many-valued logical structures, culminating in generalisations of Suszko's Thesis.
item.dc:creator: Sayantan Roy, Sankha S. Basu, Mihir K. Chakraborty

item.title: A Strong Kurepa Tree
item.description: arXiv:2507.01133v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that it is consistent that there exists a Kurepa tree $T$ such that ${}^{\omega_1}2$ is a continuous image of the topological space $[T]$ consisting of all cofinal branches of $T$ with respect to the cone topologies. This result solves an open problem due to Bergfalk, Chodounsk\'{y}, Guzm\'{a}n, and Hru\v{s}\'{a}k. We also prove that any Kurepa tree with the above property contains an Aronszajn subtree.
item.dc:creator: John Krueger

item.title: The Myhill isomorphism theorem does not generalize much
item.description: arXiv:2507.05028v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Myhill isomorphism is a variant of the Cantor-Bernstein theorem. It states that, from two injections that reduce two subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ to one another, there exists a bijection $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ that preserves them. This theorem can be proven constructively. We investigate to which extent the theorem can be extended to infinite sets other than $\mathbb{N}$. We show that, assuming Markov's principle, the theorem can be extended to the conatural numbers $\mathbb{N}_{\infty}$ provided that we only require that bicomplemented sets are preserved by the bijection. This restriction is essential. Otherwise, the picture is overall negative: among other things, it is impossible to extend that result to either $2 \times \mathbb{N}_{\infty}$, $\mathbb{N} + \mathbb{N}_{\infty}$, $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}_{\infty}$, $\mathbb{N}_{\infty}^2$, $2^{\mathbb{N}}$ or $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$.
item.dc:creator: C\'ecilia Pradic

item.title: Forcing with random variables in bounded arithmetics and set theory
item.description: arXiv:2603.10908v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyse the Boolean-valued random forcing $B_{M,\Omega}$ in bounded arithmetics developed in Krajicek (Forcing with random variables and proof complexity, vol. 382, Cambridge University Press, 2011) from the perspective of the forcing in set theory. We observe that under the assumption that $M$ is a non-standard $\omega_1$-saturated model of true arithmetics of size $\omega_1$, and $\Omega \in M$ is a non-standard number, $B_{M,\Omega}$ is isomorphic to the probability (random) algebra corresponding to the product measure space on $2^{\omega_1}$ (and hence does not depend on $M$ and $\Omega$). Thus, in a well-defined sense, the forcing $B_{M,\Omega}$ adds a "random integer" to the model $M$, using a non-separable algebra corresponding to $2^{\omega_1}$. If $G$ is a generic filter for $B_{M,\Omega}$ over a transitive model of set theory $V$, we naturally define in $V[G]$ two-valued generic extensions $M[G]^{R}$ of $M$ which correspond to Boolean-valued models in Krajicek's book (where $R$ ranges over collections of random variables which function as names for new integers). We study the relationship between the linear order $(M,<)$ and its extensions $(M[G]^R,<)$, proving several results on the extent of the mutual density of new integers in $M[G]^{R}$ and the "ground-model" integers in $M$. At the end, we discuss some advantages and limitations of interpreting forcing in bounded arithmetics (and other weak theories) in the framework of set-theoretic forcing, providing an alternative to an axiomatic approach to forcing in bounded arithmetics formulated by Atserias and M\"uller in Partially definable forcing and bounded arithmetic, Archive for Mathematical Logic 54 (2015), 1-33.
item.dc:creator: Radek Honzik

item.title: Ultrahomogeneity of monounary algebras
item.description: arXiv:2603.26616v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A structure is ultrahomogeneous if every isomorphism between finitely generated substructures can be extended to an automorphism of the structure. The aim of this paper is to provide an explicit description of ultrahomogeneous monounary algebras of arbitrary cardinalities. We also show that a monounary algebra is ultrahomogeneous if and only if it is 1-ultrahomogeneous. These results are then viewed in the context of a several related concepts, including $\omega$-categoricity, homomorphism-homogeneity, (partial-)homogeneity, and transitivity.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Quinn-Gregson

item.title: The failure of stable composition for equivalence relations in simple theories
item.description: arXiv:2606.29087v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Casanovas and Potier proved that algebraic quantification preserves stability of formulas. They also gave a nonsimple example, answering a question of Laskowski, showing that the algebraicity hypothesis cannot simply be replaced by NFCP, and asked whether a similar example exists in a simple theory. We give such an example in elementary form. The edge-set structure of the random bipartite graph has two definable equivalence relations, both stable and NFCP, whose relational composition has the order property. The resulting theory is simple and $\aleph_0$-categorical. We also prove a formal sharpness observation: every formula in every first-order theory is an existential composition of two stable NFCP formulas algebraic in the two outer variables. Consequently, closure of stable NFCP formulas under this composition characterizes stability of the whole theory.
item.dc:creator: Mostafa Mirabi

item.title: Well-Defined but Not Predetermined Persistent Mathematical Objects, Embedded Observers, and the Provability of P = N P
item.description: arXiv:2609.10864v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a foundational distinction between \emph{well-definedness} and \emph{predetermination}. A persistent mathematical or computational object may return a unique answer whenever a query is made and preserve every previously returned answer, while its answers to as-yet unqueried inputs are not represented by one completed, history-independent extension. We call such an object \emph{well-defined but non-predetermined}. We next formulate an observer-based semantics. All observers inhabit one shared computational world, their interactions modify one common global state, and they have access to one realized history. Under axioms of shared history, historical irreversibility, persistence, and historical indistinguishability, embedded observers cannot establish from the realized history alone whether its compatible extension was predetermined or progressively formed. A persistently evolutionary polynomial time computable oracle supplies a concrete example and yields a deterministic--nondeterministic separation under an explicitly history-sensitive semantics. We then derive a conditional result concerning the provability of \(P=NP\). The conclusion is an observer-relative unprovability theorem, not an unconditional proof of classical \(P\neq NP\).
item.dc:creator: Rasoul Ramezanian

item.title: Elementary modal logics and circuit complexity
item.description: arXiv:2609.10872v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A modal logic is elementary if it is sound and complete with respect to an elementary class of Kripke frames. We prove that if a finitely axiomatizable modal logic $L$ is elementary, then the validity problem for $L$, which asks whether a given finite Kripke frame validates $L$, is in the circuit complexity class uniform $\mathsf{AC}^0$. As an application, we construct infinitely many finitely axiomatizable $\mathsf{K4}$-stable logics that are not elementary. This result provides a negative answer to Problem 6.4 in [Bezhanishvili et al., 2018] for $\mathsf{K4}$-stable logics.
item.dc:creator: Tenyo Takahashi

item.title: $n$-variable theorems for dividing lines characterized by positive consistency-inconsistency configurations, and their applications to preservation problems
item.description: arXiv:2609.36394v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define a class of classes of complete first-order theories, denoted by $\mathfrak{D}_{n\text{-var}}$, using positive consistency-inconsistency configurations and generalized indiscernibles. It contains the classes of stable, simple, NIP, NTP$_1$, NTP$_2$, NATP, NCTP, NBTP, NWP, NGP, and NPM$^{(k)}$ theories. For any dividing line $D\in\mathfrak{D}_{n\text{-var}}$ and any complete first-order theory $T\notin D$, we can always find a formula $\varphi(x,y)$ witnessing $T\notin D$ with an indexed set of parameters such that the set of its instances required to be consistent has a realization whose algebraic dimension over the whole set of parameters is $|x|$. We call statements of this form $n$-variable theorems, as they may be regarded as weak versions of one-variable theorems. Under the appropriate hypotheses on $T$, we prove that $T\in D$ if and only if the corresponding theory belongs to $D$ for (i) $T^{gt}$, (ii) $T_P$, (iii) $T^{ind}$, (iv) $T^G_K$, (v) ACF$_T$, and (vi) any completion of $T^{\bar\delta,nc}_g$. These are, respectively, the theories of generic trivializations, lovely pair expansions, $H$-structure expansions, vector spaces with a dense-codense generic $K$-subspace, algebraically closed fields with a distinguished subfield, and generic non-commutative derivations of algebraically bounded fields. The $n$-variable theorem is essential in proving (i)--(v). We also prove preservation for a special case of Mordell-Lang theories. We extend the framework to a larger class $\mathfrak{D}^h_{n\text{-var}}\supseteq\mathfrak{D}_{n\text{-var}}$, capturing higher-arity dividing lines such as NOP$_k$, NFOP$_k$, and NIP$_k$ for $1<k<\omega$. The $n$-variable theorem and preservation results (ii), (iii), (iv), and (vi) also hold for this larger class, while (i) holds assuming ${\rm acl=dcl}$.
item.dc:creator: Joonhee Kim

item.title: Forcing in bounded arithmetic and set theory: analogies and differences
item.description: arXiv:2610.03919v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide a modern overview of several forcing methods in bounded arithmetic and compare them with forcing in set theory. We specifically discuss the countable forcing framework of Atserias and Muller, the restricted ultrapowers of Bydzovsky and Muller, and forcing with random variables developed by Krajicek. We illustrate these forcing arguments by reviewing the Paris--Wilkie forcing and by giving a self-contained construction of the shallow PHP model constructed by Krajicek. We observe that, from a formal point of view, Krajicek's forcing with uncountable structures can be interpreted in the framework of Atserias and Muller after a countable collapse using an LS argument. We further observe that the countable restricted ultrapowers of Bydzovsky and Muller, used to obtain models of the theory $T_{PV}$, can also be interpreted in this framework. This part serves as a primer on modern forcing methods in bounded arithmetic. In the next part, we discuss the analogies and differences between forcing in arithmetic and set theory. We embed Krajicek's Boolean-valued models into generic extensions of models of set theory, observing that the set-theoretic forcing framework can be used to interpret forcing in arithmetics. In our interpretation, set theory offers a convenient method for formalizing forcing arguments with uncountable structures. We end with a question whether analogies with set theory can facilitate the discovery of new uncountable partial orders for arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Radek Honzik, Ondrej Je\v{z}il, Mykyta Narusevych

item.title: Coherent risk from finite models
item.description: arXiv:2602.00784v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Coherent estimators at different sample sizes need not describe the same population risk. We prove that dyadic estimators do so exactly when duplicating every scenario leaves the estimate unchanged, and recover the population dual set from the finite models. The risk of a Bernoulli loss determines the exact Wasserstein, Kolmogorov and total-variation moduli on a common bounded support. It also characterises uniform estimability, with an impossibility bound for arbitrary randomised estimators. An intrinsic floor on tail levels gives an explicit optimal Lipschitz constant and a uniform approximation defect; every deterministic vanishing floor preserves pointwise strong consistency. A nonstandard construction supplies compatible estimators at all finite sample sizes, explicit block-sum weights, and a formula for the worst-case mass created by infinitesimal tail levels. Finally, we derive uniform regret bounds for data-driven risk-averse optimisation and specialise them to stop-loss retention. Exact binomial calculations compare regularised and original estimators against the same population target.
item.dc:creator: Tomasz Kania

item.title: Classification of bipartite observables I: stable and uniformly stable observables
item.description: arXiv:2610.11002v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This is the first of a series of three papers that bring model theory to quantum information. The dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory, which separate the tame first-order theories from the wild ones, become properties of bipartite observables: properties of the expectation values obtained when two independently prepared quantum systems are idealized one after the other. In this paper we focus on stability. An observable is stable when the order in which the two systems are idealized never changes its expectation value, and this is Shelah's stability. Its classical characterizations, in model theory and in analysis, acquire a physical meaning: idealized preparations are simulated by finite mixtures of actual ones, and adaptive probes can tell apart only polynomially many preparations.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Due\~nez, Jos\'e Iovino

item.title: 86 unknowns for Hilbert's tenth problem over the rationals
item.description: arXiv:2610.20691v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recently, Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers was solved negatively by OpenAI based on a five-contact height estimate and a pole-parity construction. In this paper, we prove further that there is no algorithm to decide for any polynomial $P(x_1,\ldots,x_{86})$ with integer coefficients whether the equation $P(x_1,\ldots,x_{86})=0$ has solutions with $x_1,\ldots,x_{86}\in\mathbb Q$.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Wei Sun
